Project 
 The Woodfibre LNG Project is located approximately 7 km west-southwest of Squamish, British Columbia. It involves the construction and operation of a liquefied natural gas (LNG) export facility on the previous Woodfibre pulp mill site, which would have a storage capacity of 250,000 m3 and would produce approximately 2.1 million tons per year of LNG.
 Woodfibre Management Ltd. is a privately held Canadian company based in Vancouver and a subsidiary of Pacific Energy Corporation Limited.
 Job Summary 
 Woodfibre LNG is seeking an experienced Analyzer Technician to join our dynamic team. Reporting to the Electrical & Instrumentation Supervisor , the successful candidate will support preventive, predictive, corrective, turnaround, and emergency maintenance activities. Key responsibilities include installing, calibrating, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing process analyzers, analyzer sample conditioning systems, and associated instrumentation to ensure accurate and reliable process measurements. The successful candidate will also provide support for general instrumentation maintenance & Turnaround activities as required. This role offers an opportunity to be part of a dedicated team, ensuring the safe, reliable, efficient, and environmentally responsible operation of the Woodfibre LNG facility.
 Key Responsibilities : 
 The successful applicant will:
 Support start-up and operations of the LNG plant 
 Troubleshoot and repair process analyzers such as Gas Chromatographs, Continuous Emissions Monitoring Systems (CEMS), Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP) analyzers, moisture analyzers, oxygen analyzers, and associated analyzer sample conditioning systems.
 Troubleshoot and repair ABB PGC5000 and PGC1000 Gas Chromatographs, ABB AO2000 Continuous Emissions Monitoring System (CEMS), ABB RVP4501 Analyzer, and associated analyzer equipment.
 Assist with the maintenance, troubleshooting, calibration, and repair of other process instrumentation and control systems, as required, to support plant operations and maintenance activities.
 Utilize remote connectivity and digital support platforms, as required, to perform diagnostics, configuration, testing, troubleshooting, and maintenance of analyzer systems in collaboration with Operations, Engineering, OEMs, and third-party service providers
 Support Process Safety Management - Maintain analyzer systems that support process safety, environmental compliance, and operational integrity. SIS awareness, Alarm philosophy, Functional Safety
 Inspect, test, calibrate, and validate analyzer systems to ensure accurate and reliable process measurements using electrical, electronic, pneumatic, and analytical testing equipment.
 Perform scheduled preventive, predictive, and emergency maintenance on analyzer systems, completing all maintenance reports, calibration records, and equipment history documentation.
 Perform mechanical work associated with analyzer repair and modification, including the removal and installation of tubing, sample lines, regulators, filters, sample conditioning equipment, and analyzer components.
 Perform analyzer calibration using certified calibration gases and reference standards while maintaining measurement accuracy and compliance with manufacturer recommendations.
 Troubleshoot analyzer communication interfaces with the ICSS, PLCs, and associated control systems.
 Provide day-to-day support to ensure maximum reliability and availability of analyzer systems while working towards achieving plant reliability goals and measuring the effectiveness of maintenance programs.
 Review process flow diagrams, analyzer drawings, sample system drawings, equipment lists, and technical specifications to develop and execute maintenance activities.
 Collaborate with Operations, Engineering, Reliability, and third-party analyzer service providers to support plant performance and reliability.
 Contribute to the continuous improvement of maintenance key performance indicators.
 HSSE 
 100% compliance with company HSE policies and guidelines.
 Champion HSE as a member of the LNG Operations Team.
 Lead HSE Shift Meeting/ safety walks/audits if and when required.
 Timely intervention to mitigate risks and ensure the safety of personnel and plant.
 Demonstrate a personal commitment to influence overall safety behavior in the plant.
 Safeguarding systems check lists are implemented/completed by Shift Operations to agreed frequencies and standards.
 Execute plant wide operations hazards awareness program. 
 Initiate inputs for plant risk register and mitigation tracking process for operations.
 Required Experience 
 Minimum of 5+ years of relevant industrial maintenance experience.
 A valid BC Journeyman Instrumentation Technician Certificate or Red Seal Instrumentation Technician certification. Dual ticket would be an asset. 
 Experience with ABB PGC5000, ABB PGC1000, ABB AO2000 CEMS, and ABB RVP4501 analyzers.
 Experience with analyzer sample conditioning systems and calibration gas systems.
 Knowledge of regulatory requirements in BC
 Proficiency with Yokogawa control systems.
 Commissioning and start-up experience.
 Knowledge of DCS systems, PLCs, HMI systems, and industrial communications.
 Experience with analyzer calibration, validation, and troubleshooting.
 Previous experience using a Project Resource Manager (PRM) and Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS), such as SAP.
 Additional Requirements 
 Energetic in pursuit of continuous improvement processes.
 Experience working with large multi-disciplinary teams, and contractors in a multicultural environment is an asset. 
 Communication/interpersonal skills – to be able to interact with front line workers through to management and all hierarchical levels. 
 Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
 Motivated and willing to take ownership of tasks.
 Ability to work well under pressure and handle multiple tasks, targets and changing priorities within tight time frames.
 Shares knowledge readily and encourages personal development.
 Demonstrated computer knowledge with experience in Microsoft Outlook, Word, and Excel, etc.
 A valid driver’s license (with abstract) and passport.
 Must be legally entitled to work in Canada.
 This role will be a combination of office and site-based role.
 The position is based in Squamish, BC (Project Site), and work in the Company’s Vancouver Office as required . 
 Only qualified candidates legally entitled to work in Canada will be contacted. 
 Thank you in advance for your interest!

HELLO!

I’m Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. I’m excited to share that we’re hiring our first Support Engineering Manager in AMER.

Support Engineering is the technical bridge between frontline Support, Product, and Engineering. The team investigates complex product and customer issues, helps confirm which problems truly require code changes, and enables the broader Support organization to resolve more issues independently. We’re looking for a hands-on leader to make that bridge stronger as the function grows—aligning technical rigor with Ashby’s broader standards for customer success.

This is not a traditional Support Manager role. You’ll manage and mentor Support Engineers, stay close to complex investigations, and work with Engineering and Product to improve how technical issues are diagnosed, escalated, and resolved. You’ll help define the standards and systems that let a small, highly technical team move quickly without sacrificing judgment or quality.




ABOUT THE ROLE

When a complex issue moves beyond frontline Support, Support Engineering investigates the problem using customer context, application behavior, logs, databases, integrations, APIs, and code-level context. The team determines whether the issue can be resolved through configuration, data correction, documentation, enablement, or an in-app change—or whether it is a product defect that Engineering needs to fix. Your role is to make that path clearer and more effective: develop a deep understanding of how each partner team works, coach the investigation, and ensure escalations meet a shared standard for evidence, ownership, and customer impact.

You’ll lead the team’s day-to-day technical development while building the connective tissue around it. That includes reviewing investigations and escalations, mentoring Support Engineers through ambiguous problems, clarifying triage and handoff practices, identifying recurring patterns, and partnering with frontline Support, Product, and Engineering on durable improvements. You’ll help ensure Support Engineering scales in a way that reflects Ashby’s broader expectations for customer success—not simply by passing issues between teams, but by resolving more issues independently and making the right problems easier for Engineering to act on.

As the first Support Engineering Manager at Ashby, you’ll have meaningful influence over how the function grows. You’ll balance people leadership with hands-on technical judgment, make pragmatic decisions with incomplete information, and focus the team on the work that most improves customer outcomes, strengthens cross-functional trust, and protects Engineering time.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN

 - Lead, coach, and develop Support Engineers through regular feedback, technical mentorship, career development, and clear expectations for ownership and judgment.

 - Stay close to complex investigations by reviewing technical work, joining escalations when useful, and coaching the team on APIs, integrations, logs, databases, data issues, configuration, and product behavior.

 - Build shared operating standards across Support, Support Engineering, Product, and Engineering that help frontline Support resolve more issues independently, reduce customer effort, and ensure Engineering receives clear, actionable escalations when code changes are needed.

 - Partner with Engineering and Product to synthesize recurring customer patterns, validate defects, improve supportability, and determine whether the right solution is a code change, documentation, tooling, enablement, or process improvement.

 - Identify the highest-leverage friction in the team’s workflows and ship practical improvements to tooling, diagnostics, routing, documentation, and operating processes.

 - Hire and onboard future Support Engineers, help define the team’s career path, and build a scalable model for technical growth as the function expands across regions.

 - Track and improve the outcomes that matter: resolution speed, escalation quality, frontline self-sufficiency, customer effort, recurring issue reduction, and Engineering time spent on confirmed defects and roadmap work.


YOU SHOULD APPLY IF

 - You have direct people-management experience leading a technical support, developer support, production support, or support engineering team in a B2B SaaS or similarly complex software environment.

 - You are energized by hands-on people leadership: reviewing work, giving precise feedback, raising technical judgment, and helping strong engineers grow.

 - You have coached an Engineer through a specific technical or judgment gap and can point to what changed as a result.

 - You have enough technical depth to reason about APIs, integrations, logs, databases, application behavior, and code-level context—and to coach others through ambiguous investigations.

 - You know how to distinguish a configuration, data, documentation, or enablement issue from a true product defect, and can help a team make that decision with evidence.

 - You have improved an escalation, triage, or support-to-Engineering workflow and can explain what changed, why you changed it, and how you measured the result.

 - You build structure without over-engineering. You can make clear decisions with incomplete information, ship a useful first version, and iterate based on what you learn. You’ve stood up processes, workflows, or standards from scratch.

 - You communicate clearly and thoughtfully with technical and non-technical audiences, especially when explaining tradeoffs, uncertainty, customer impact, and recommended action.


YOU SHOULD NOT APPLY IF

 - You have not yet directly managed a team, and your leadership experience has primarily been through mentorship, project leadership, or team-lead responsibilities. This role requires direct people-management experience, including accountability for team development, feedback, and day-to-day management.

 - You’re looking primarily for a traditional queue-management or people-management role where you can stay removed from technical investigations and escalation quality.

 - Most of your experience is in internal IT, help desk, endpoint, infrastructure, cloud operations, or systems administration without substantial experience debugging customer-impacting SaaS applications and integrations.

 - You prefer to optimize processes from a distance rather than work directly with engineers on the details of diagnosis, evidence, and technical judgment.

 - You see Support Engineering primarily as a pass-through queue to Engineering rather than an investigation and enablement layer that should resolve more issues independently.

 - You’re uncomfortable operating in a growing function where ownership boundaries, workflows, and success measures will continue to evolve.

 - You prefer prolonged analysis or perfect certainty over making a well-reasoned decision, learning quickly, and improving the system in motion.

 L'associé(e) du support premium fonctionne en première ligne et interagit directement avec les clients et les parties prenantes internes. Les associés du support premium ont besoin de solides compétences en communication, de capacités de résolution de problèmes et d'une expertise en matière de service client. Ils doivent également être adaptables et réactifs dans notre environnement en évolution rapide, parfois sous pression, tout en restant flexibles, proactifs, ingénieux, efficaces et démontrant un haut niveau de professionnalisme et de confidentialité.

 Gestion de cas complexes : Fournir le plus haut niveau de service à notre communauté dans chaque cas 
 Interagir avec les clients Airbnb et les membres de la communauté via tous les canaux actuels et futurs, à la fois à l'intérieur et à l'extérieur des outils Airbnb, y compris le chat en direct, les plateformes sociales, la messagerie et directement par téléphone.
 S'approprier de bout en bout tous les cas assignés : garantir qu'une résolution finale complète (ou un règlement, une décision finale, etc.) est atteinte sur la base des flux de travail et des directives de gestion, en favorisant la relation avec nos utilisateurs tout au long du processus et en les transmettant avec précision aux autres équipes le cas échéant.
 Démontrer une mentalité de propriétaire et un bon jugement ainsi que la capacité de remettre en question et de s'écarter du flux de travail lorsque cela est nécessaire uniquement avec l'approbation de la direction.
 Être très réceptif aux retours de la Direction et de la Qualité, et adopter rapidement des comportements pour améliorer la qualité de votre travail.
 Comprendre plusieurs perspectives sur un sujet ou une situation et est capable d'évaluer et de présenter plusieurs options pour résoudre un problème.
 Peut être amené à s'engager davantage avec les parties prenantes de haut niveau et à collaborer de manière interfonctionnelle, avec l'aide de la direction.

 Afficher une capacité à traiter un plus grand volume de cas sans impact négatif sur la qualité de l'interaction et la résolution.
 Anticiper et identifier de manière proactive les opportunités d'améliorer l'expérience utilisateur et, avec le soutien de la direction, proposer des solutions et des recommandations sur mesure qui vont au-delà de leurs attentes, et garantir une expérience fluide et mémorable tout au long de leurs interactions avec Airbnb.
 Résoudre les problèmes des utilisateurs rapidement et avec un niveau élevé de satisfaction mutuelle, en tenant compte du contexte et des circonstances spécifiques.
 Personnaliser les communications avec les utilisateurs, en démontrant les normes d'hospitalité les plus élevées.

 Fournir des informations sur l'expérience de la communauté et les opportunités d'amélioration continue à votre direction.

 Fournir des services techniques/fonctionnels/SME aux membres les moins expérimentés de l'équipe.
 Partager des idées pour améliorer les processus et les méthodes de travail.

 Empathie et patience dans les relations avec les clients, en particulier dans les situations de haute pression

 Passion pour offrir un service client exceptionnel et placer la barre haute
 Capacité à prospérer dans un environnement ambigu, rapide et complexe, en agissant de manière proactive pour réagir rapidement et de manière décisive.

 About the Storage Execution team
 The Storage Execution team sits at the heart of MongoDB’s Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) team. We own the core transactional read/write path on each node, across both today’s storage engine and a next‑generation cloud-native storage architecture. Our work determines how correct and performant MongoDB is for customers running mission-critical production workloads.

 Defining and maintaining the internal collection and index APIs used by Replication, Query and Catalog modules, and commands for local reads and writes, plus the transaction and durability primitives that govern visibility, conflict resolution and crash recovery
 Integrating the next generation of MongoDB’s storage architecture into the server in a way that is predictable for other teams, scales with cloud elasticity, and preserves the performance and safety of the classic configuration
 Improving transaction processing speed and semantics of both single shard and cross-shard transactions
 Owning index builds and schema‑level storage operations (build/rebuild, cleanup, resumability) and ensuring they behave well for large, highly available clusters running write-heavy workloads
 Building validation, diagnostics, and storage‑focused test infrastructure to catch durability issues early and keep the system trustworthy at scale
 Partnering with neighboring teams on flow control, prioritization and load-shedding to stay within resource limits, protecting durability and availability at the cluster level without starving critical operations

 Own the team’s roadmap across durability, availability, performance, and developer productivity, in partnership with OLTP leadership and Product Management
 Manage customer escalations involving storage behavior and durability; work directly with Support, Atlas, and other server teams to reproduce, root‑cause, and resolve issues
 Drive process and tooling improvements that raise engineering velocity and code quality (e.g., ownership, review expectations, customer escalation and build failure practices)
 Partner closely with Replication, Query, Sharding, Catalog & Routing, Storage Engines, and Atlas teams on cross‑team features such as the new storage architecture, availability improvements, and workload management

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any.  You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.  Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.  We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere.  We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.
